evidence.section: 3.3 Effect of annealing on structure and microhardness
evidence.quote: Annealing at a lower temperature of 1000°C drastically changes the structure of the Fe 36 Mn 21 Cr 18 Ni 15 Al 10 alloy

The Fe 36 Mn 21 Cr 18 Ni 15 Al 10 alloy ... was produced by vacuum arc melting of the high-purity (at least 99.9%) constitutive elements. The produced ingot had dimensions of ~10 х15x60 mm 3. The ingot was remelted 5 times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
Some specimens were annealed either at 1000°C or 1200°C for 24 hours in vaccumized quartz tubes and cooled down on air.

evidence.section: 3.1 Structure of the Fe36Mn21Cr18Ni15Al10 alloy in the as-cast condition
evidence.quote: The TEM analysis (Fig. 1c-d) confirms the presence of cuboidal second phase particles with the average size of 160±30 nm. The volume fraction of the second phase particles is 50%. The analysis of the selected area electron diffraction patterns (insert in Fig. 1d) has revealed that the particles have an ordered bcc B2 structure, while the matrix phase has a disordered bcc structure.

evidence.section: 3.1 Structure of the Fe36Mn21Cr18Ni15Al10 alloy in the as-cast condition
evidence.quote: The TEM analysis (Fig. 1c-d) confirms the presence of cuboidal second phase particles with the average size of 160±30 nm. The volume fraction of the second phase particles is 50%. The analysis of the selected area electron diffraction patterns (insert in Fig. 1d) has revealed that the particles have an ordered bcc B2 structure, while the matrix phase has a disordered bcc structure.

After annealing at 1200°C the general appearance of the microstructure remains similar to that in the as-cast condition (Fig. 3a). The XRD analysis (not shown) also does not reveal noticeable changes.

the second (B2) phase particles attain almost perfect cuboidal shape with straight interphase boundaries, and the fraction of B2 phase decreases to 39%. The size of B2 phase particles is larger than in the as-cast condition - 220±40 nm.

attributes.composition: almost nominal composition of the alloy with fine B2 particles

evidence.quote: The volume fractions of the bcc, B2, and fcc phases are 41%, 30%, and 29% respectively.

attributes.size: coarse B2 particles 5-10 µm; fine B2 particles ~0.35 µm
attributes.location: precipitate-free areas along initial bcc grain boundaries contain coarse B2; fine B2 in bcc matrix
attributes.composition: coarse B2 primarily Ni and Al

evidence.quote: In the vicinity of these areas coarse B2 particles with the average sizes of 5-10 µm are found. The shape of fine B2 particles becomes much more irregular in comparison with the as-cast condition, and their size increases to ~0.35 µm. ... The volume fractions of the bcc, B2, and fcc phases are 41%, 30%, and 29% respectively.

attributes.location: precipitate-free areas along initial bcc grain boundaries

evidence.quote: XRD (not shown) and EBSD analysis (Fig. 3c) reveals the presence of an fcc phase in addition to the bcc and B2 (EBSD does not distinguish bcc and ordered B2 phases due to limited sensitivity). Moreover, EBSD phase map suggests that the precipitate free-areas visible in the SEM-BSE image (Fig. 3b) have fcc structure. Chemical composition analysis (Table 3) demonstrates that the fcc phase is enriched with Fe and Mn ... The volume fractions of the bcc, B2, and fcc phases are 41%, 30%, and 29% respectively.
At room temperature, the alloy demonstrates relatively high yield strength of 990 MPa in compression.
The alloy had high compression yield strength of 940-990 MPa at temperatures up to 400°C.
At room temperature the Fe 36 Mn 21 Cr 18 Ni 15 Al 10 alloy has in tension the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength of 750 and 880 MPa respectively (Fig. 2a, Table 2).

but had a limited tensile ductility, especially at room temperature – elongation to fracture was only 2.5%.
The alloy also demonstrates moderate ductility with an elongation to fracture of 20%.
The measured density of the alloy is 7.18 g/cm 3.
A slight increase of microhardness by ~30 HV due to annealing at 1200°C is also observed (Table 4).
Structural transformations after annealing at 1000°C are accompanied with the prominent decrease of microhardness down to 310 HV (Table 4).

The TEM analysis (Fig. 1c-d) confirms the presence of cuboidal second phase particles with the average size of 160±30 nm.
After annealing at 1000°C an additional fcc phase appeared. The formation of the fcc phase caused pronounced softening.
